We need to find template that when applied to the molecule (product) reproduces the Doebner modification retrosynthesis. The input from previous step gave precursors: ["CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccccc1N", "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc2)cc1"] Wait that seems odd: The product is the second SMILES? Actually previous step: make_7_lvl2-apply_template-1 asked: "Can you return all possible precursors of applying the template as the result of the task make_7_lvl2-template_search-1 to the molecule below?" Answer gave list of two SMILES: first is "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccccc1N" and second is "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc2)cc1". So the target molecule is likely the second? Actually they applied a template to some molecule and got precursors. The target molecule is likely the one from make_7_lvl2-template_search-1. We need to find the template that when applied to the molecule reproduces the reaction described (Doebner modification). The product of Doebner is an alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. In our case, the product SMILES likely contains C=CC(=O)O attached to aromatic ring. Indeed second SMILES: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc2)cc1". That is a sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings, one with a C=CC(=O)O side chain (alpha,beta-unsaturated acid). So the target is that molecule. The precursors from template application are: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccccc1N" (maybe a protected amine?) and the same target? Wait the list includes the target itself? Actually the second SMILES is same as target, so maybe the template didn't change? Might be misinterpretation.

We need to find the template ID and mapped_rxn. We can search templates that match the target and have functional groups broken/formed as described. Use get_available_functional_groups to see correct names.
